newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australian Telstra Corp opens Indonesian company.
newsitem.headline: Australian Telstra Corp opens Indonesian company.

text.p: Australian telecommunications giant Telstra Corp launched on Monday a wholly-owned Indonesian company and said it saw great growth potential for its operations in the country.
Ross Abbott, president director of PT Telstra Nusantara, said the new venture would increase Telstra's presence in the Indonesian market where it previously only had two representative offices.
"It will be a big improvement from the representative offices where more decisions had to be referred to Australia," Abbott said.

He said Telstra had been operating in Indonesia for around five years. It currently had a 20 percent stake in a consortium to build 400,000 new subscriber lines in central Java and a 75 percent share of a private mobile radio venture.
Abbott said the new company would take advantage of growth areas in Indonesia in consulting for private companies and bidding for line construction contracts.

"Penetration of telephone services is low (in Indonesia) if you compare it to GDP per capita," he said, adding that there was great scope for telecommunication network growth in a country of over 13,000 islands.
Abbott added that Telstra would also be looking at expanding its role in providing "high class" services such as the Internet which were increasingly demanded by Indonesia's burgeoning middle class.
"We are interested in providing telecommunications but we will do that in partnership with strong local partners," he said.
